tasks.question: What is a 'Transition' in a presentation?
options: An effect applied to an object on a slide
The visual effect when moving from one slide to the next
The background color of a slide

tasks.question: What is an 'Animation' in a presentation?
options: Moving from one slide to another
Visual effects applied to individual elements on a slide
The music playing in the background

tasks.question: Which of these is an 'Entrance' animation?
What is an 'Exit' animation?
options: Making an object disappear from the slide
Making an object move in a circle

tasks.question: What is an 'Emphasis' animation?
options: Bringing an object onto the slide
Drawing attention to an object already on the slide

tasks.question: What is a 'Motion Path'?
options: An animation that moves an object along a specific line or shape
The file path on the hard drive

tasks.question: How do you preview an animation?
options: Clicking the 'Preview' button on the Animations tab

tasks.question: What does 'Duration' mean in animation?
options: How long the animation takes to complete

tasks.question: What does 'Delay' mean in animation?
options: The time to wait before the animation begins

tasks.question: What is the 'Animation Pane' used for?
options: To manage and reorder the animations on a slide

tasks.question: What is a 'Trigger' in animation?
options: Something that causes an animation to start (like a click)

tasks.question: What does 'On Click' mean for starting an animation?
options: The animation starts when you click the mouse or press a key
The animation starts after the previous one

tasks.question: What does 'With Previous' mean?
options: The animation starts at the same time as the one before it
The animation starts after the one before it
The animation starts only on the first slide

tasks.question: What does 'After Previous' mean?
options: The animation starts at the same time
The animation starts immediately after the previous effect finishes
The animation starts when you click
The animation starts at the end of the show

tasks.question: Why should you avoid too many flashy transitions?
options: They can distract the audience from your message

tasks.question: Which of these is a common slide transition?
What is 'Morph' transition in modern PowerPoint?
options: A smooth transition that animates objects from one slide to their position on the next

tasks.question: Can you apply a transition to all slides at once?
options: Only if there are fewer than 5 slides

tasks.question: What is 'Reorder Animation'?
options: Changing the sequence in which objects animate

tasks.question: What is an 'Effect Option'?
options: Adjusting specific details of an animation, like direction

tasks.question: What is 'Advance Slide' setting?
options: Deciding if the slide changes on click or after a certain time

tasks.question: Can animations have sound effects?
What is the primary goal of using animations?
options: To control the flow of information and emphasize key points
To use every feature of the software

tasks.question: Which tab is used to add slide-to-slide effects?
What happens if you set duration to 0.01 seconds?

tasks.text: Transitions occur between two different slides.
Animations are applied to objects on a slide.
Entrance effects bring objects onto the screen.
The Animation Pane shows all effects on a slide.
Duration controls how long an effect lasts.
Click 'Apply to All' for consistent transitions.
Exit effects make objects disappear from view.
Motion paths move objects along a set route.
Too many animations can distract your audience.
Emphasis effects highlight specific slide content.
